sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc-Lko:4881
Court No. - 15
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 12344 of 2023

Applicant :- Neha Trivedi @ Amna Begum
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P Thru. Cbi. Acb Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Deepak Kumar Bhola
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Anurag Kumar Singh
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the accused-applicant, as well as Mr. Dharmendra Pratap Singh,
Advocate, holding brief of Mr. Anurag Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the respondent- CBI and,
perused the record.

2. This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Neha Trivedi @ Amna Begum for grant of bail in FIR No/RC-8(A)/2007 dated 31.03.2007, C.C.No.01A/2010, under Sections 120-B,
419, 420, 467, 468 and 471 IPC read with Sections 13(2) r/w 13(1)(d) P.C. Act, 1988 lodged at Police Station CBI/ACB, Lucknow, during trial.

3. Learned counsel for the accused-applicant, while pressing the bail application, submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this case and, she has not committed any offence, as claimed by the prosecution.

It is further submitted that the role which has been assigned to the applicant in the alleged commission of crime is to the tune that she in connivance with the other accused persons Neha Trivedi @ Amna Begum vs State Of U.P Thru. Cbi.

sentences.text: Acb Lko.

1 of the alleged crime has hatched a criminal conspiracy and in furtherance to the same loan was taken from the bank and she was also instrumental in opening a fake bank-account in the name of Amna Begum in Bank of India, Kaushalpuri Branch, Kanpur wherein the money was siphoned and was ultimately withdrawn.

It is vehemently submitted that the charge-sheet in this case was filed way back in the year 2009, however, the applicant was not arrested during the course of investigation and thereafter the applicant could not get any knowledge of any process issued by the trial Court as is also evident from the rejection order passed by the trial Court and she is shown to have been arrested by the police from Dehradun after issuance of process under Section 82-83 CrPC.
4.
It is next submitted that applicant is languishing in jail in this case since 10.09.2023 and she is a lady.

It is further submitted that the identically placed co-accused persons- Surya Kant Mishra alias Naveen Varshney, Vinod Kumar Srivastava and Naresh Chandra Bhardwaj have been enlarged on bail by the trial Courts concerned.

entities.text: Surya Kant Mishra alias Naveen Varshney
entities.label: OTHER_PERSON

sentences.text: The applicant is not having any previous criminal history.
Charge sheet in this case has already been filed and there is no apprehension that after being released on bail, she may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent- CBI, however, vehemently opposes the prayer of bail of the applicant but could not confront the submissions made on behalf of the applicant that identically placed co-accused persons- Surya Kant Mishra alias Naveen Varshney, Vinod Kumar Srivastava and Naresh Chandra Bhardwaj have been enlarged on bail by the trial Courts concerned.

entities.text: Surya Kant Mishra alias Naveen Varshney
entities.label: OTHER_PERSON

sentences.text: 6. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it prima facie appears that the other accused persons, namely, identically placed co-accused persons- Surya Kant Mishra alias Naveen Varshney, Vinod Kumar Srivastava and Naresh Chandra Bhardwaj who have been assigned identical role in commission of the crime, have been granted bail by the trial Courts concerned.

entities.text: Surya Kant Mishra alias Naveen Varshney
entities.label: OTHER_PERSON

sentences.text: The bail application of the applicant appears to have been rejected by the trial Court only on the ground that despite various processes issued against her, including process under Section 82-83 CrPC, she did not appear before the trial Court and has been arrested from Dehradun.

The defence of the applicant appears to be that prior to issuance of process under Section 82-83 CrPC,
no process of the trial Court was ever served on her.
Be that as it may, the applicant is a lady and similarly situated accused persons are enjoying the benefit of bail.

She is also not having any criminal antecedents to her credit and apprehension of the CBI pertaining to non-availability of the applicant before the trial Court may be taken care of by placing adequate conditions on her.
7. In result, the bail application moved on behalf of the applicant - Neha Trivedi @ Amna Begum is hereby allowed.

8. Let the accused/applicant-Neha Trivedi @ Amna Begum, involved in above-mentioned case, be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 02 Lakh with two sureties of the same amount, one of the surety would be a blood relative of the applicant, subject to following conditions:-
Neha Trivedi @ Amna Begum vs State Of U.P Thru. Cbi. Acb Lko.

2 (i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
9. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
10. Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the Court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

11. Observations made herein-above by this court are only for the purpose of disposal of this bail application and shall not be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
